title: Free a riser that is sitting on a pencil, without spilling the open jar on it
instruction: The riser under the open jar of varnish is sitting on a pencil. Get it sitting flat on the table where it is, with the jar still on it.
context: Anything set down on a stray pencil or offcut rocks, and whatever stands on it leans. The pencil is pinned by the load: pulling it drags the riser and the open jar along, and lifting the riser carelessly tips the jar, so one hand takes the weight off that side while the other clears the pencil.
setup: Six loose objects on the table. Positions are (x, y) in cm: x forward from the line joining the two arm bases, y to the left of the midline between the arms (the bases are at y = +30.5 and -30.5). Task objects: (1) Dark-stained oak riser, a solid block 26 x 7 x 4 cm, 0.50 kg, lying on its 26 x 7 cm face with its long side pointing straight away from the arms, centred at (27, 0): near end at x = 14, far end at x = 40. (2) Yellow wooden pencil, 17.5 cm long, 7 mm across, 6 g, lying at right angles to the riser at x = 25, from y = -2 to y = -19.5, so its tip is 1.5 cm under the riser's right-hand long edge and the other 16 cm sticks out to the right. (3) Open glass jar of varnish: a clear straight-sided 8 oz drinking glass, 6.6 cm across and 10 cm tall, 0.30 kg with its contents, standing on the riser's top with its centre at (31, 0), on the riser's centreline 9 cm from the far end. Because of the pencil the riser rests on its left bottom edge and the pencil tip: its right bottom edge is 8 mm off the table, and the riser and the jar lean 7 degrees to the left. Distractors, not part of the task and ignored by scoring: (4) red ceramic mug, 9 cm across (11.4 cm with handle), 8 cm tall, 0.30 kg, at (48, +25), handle toward the arms; (5) roll of brown packing tape, 10 cm across, 5 cm tall, 0.06 kg, lying flat at (51, +12); (6) Phillips screwdriver, 19 cm long, 3.4 cm across the handle, 0.10 kg, lying left-right at x = 48 from y = -15 (handle end) to y = +4 (tip).
scoring: 0 if at any time the jar tilts more than 15 degrees from vertical (varnish over the rim); putting things right afterwards does not undo this. Otherwise, judged at the end with the riser, jar and pencil all at rest and no gripper finger within 2 cm of any of them: 1.0 if all four bottom corners of the riser are within 2 mm of the table, the riser's centre is within 1 cm of where it started and its long side within 5 degrees of straight away from the arms, the jar stands on the riser's top (base centre inside its outline, lowest point within 4 mm of the face) within 3 degrees of vertical, and, seen from above, no part of the pencil is within 2 cm of the riser. 0.5 if the riser is flat (same 2 mm test), the jar stands on it within 3 degrees of vertical and, seen from above, the pencil does not overlap the riser, but the riser's centre has moved more than 1 cm, or it has turned more than 5 degrees, or the pencil lies within 2 cm of it. 0 in every other case, including doing nothing, the pencil still under the riser or lying on it, a corner more than 2 mm off the table, the jar not on the riser, a gripper still holding anything, or the riser, jar or pencil still moving. Lifting the jar off and putting it back upright is allowed. A full score must hold for 3 s. The distractors are not scored.
reset_notes: Place the pencil first, then set the riser down with its right edge on the pencil tip, then stand the jar on it. Real trials can use water in the jar; wipe up any spill before the next trial.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, uniform rubber-like friction (1.2/1.0), higher than wood on a bench, so the pinned pencil drags the riser more readily. Riser is a plain box (corners stand in for feet); pencil a square bar that cannot roll (no SimReady pencil). Jar is an empty SimReady 8 oz glass, convex hull, 0.30 kg for glass plus varnish. Varnish not simulated: tilt past 15 degrees counts as a spill; slopping from a jolt is not modelled. No force sensing.
